root_cause:
H3 is the answer, and H1/H2 are the reason H3 was never noticed. Cover is published only by a renderer that calls `markTowerCover` at its sprite commit. There are exactly THREE production publish sites — `towerRenderer.ts:313` (the 12 race towers, gated on `towerArtForRecipe`), `structureRampRenderer.ts:223` (the 5 RAMP_SPECS towers, reached from BOTH `world.creatureSpawners` and `world.defenders`) and `voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:576` (the Voltkin chain). `stinkTowerRenderer.ts` draws the tower — from its own shipped veo atlas — and calls `markTowerCover` ZERO times.

H1 is HALF right and the half that is wrong matters: S183's defender loop DOES walk the stink tower. `structureRampRenderer.ts:266` iterates `world.defenders.values()`, which contains every stink tower. It then bails one line later at `structureRampRenderer.ts:268` — `if (spec === null) continue; // the stink tower, which has no ramp art` — because `rampSpecFor('stinkTower')` returns null. So the collection reaches it and the RAMP_SPECS gate turns it away. H2 is therefore the precise mechanism (no RAMP_SPECS entry), but H2's premise — "cover is only published by the ramp path" — is false: three paths publish, and the stink tower is outside all three.

⭐ THE HEADLINE: the stink tower is the ONLY buildable structure in the game whose shapes are still visible. `ALL_BLUEPRINT_IDS` (`blueprints.ts:376-390`) holds 19 recipes: 6 tier-3 race towers + 6 tier-9 boss towers (all 12 covered by `towerRenderer`), 5 RAMP_SPECS towers (covered by `structureRampRenderer`), `voltkin` (covered by `voltkinTowerRenderer`) — 18 — and `stinkTower`. He is exactly right that it is "the one tower you forgot".

⚠ `structureRamp.ts:13`'s "the eight remaining towers are still his call" is about RAMP ART, not about cover, and reading it as a cover count is the trap in question 7. Seven of those eight (6 race towers + voltkin) already publish cover from their own renderers.

evidence.quote: if (spec === null) continue; // the stink tower, which has no ramp art
evidence.why_it_matters: THE DECISIVE LINE. S183's defender loop (:266 `for (const def of world.defenders.values())`) does reach the stink tower — it is turned away one line later by the RAMP_SPECS gate, by name, in a comment. This settles H1 vs H2: the loop covers it, the gate refuses it.

This file is the renderer that actually draws the tower he sees, and a full read of it (280 lines) contains NO `markTowerCover` call anywhere. `grep -rn "markTowerCover" src --include=*.ts` returns exactly three production call sites and this file is not one of them. H3 CONFIRMED.

⛔⛔ THE MONEY ANSWER (question 3). The publish API takes ids and a tick. NOTHING about art, atlases, frames or geometry. Publishing cover does NOT structurally require ramp art. Any renderer that can name the shapes a building stands on can publish, and the stink tower renderer already has `d.anchorPrimitiveId` in hand.

THE ART ALREADY SHIPS. `stink-tower-atlas.png` is on disk at 3060×480 (12 cols × 255, 2 rows × 240), 1.29 MB, loaded by `stinkTowerRenderer.ensureAtlas` (:105-131) since S151 P3. ZERO generation spend. This is why the fix is small.

THE SPRITE-COMMIT POINT — where `markTowerCover` belongs. It is already downstream of the fog skip (:148 `if (isConcealed(...)) continue;`) and of the atlas gate (:167 `if (this.atlas !== null)`), so publishing here honours the towerCover contract (*'never above the fog skip or the atlas bail'*) for free, with no restructuring.

evidence.why_it_matters: THE TRAP, MEASURED HONESTLY. The fallback shape scan (:830-844) never consults cover alpha, so an INVISIBLE shape is still clickable — the tower does not become mechanically unreachable. `radius` is `Math.max(8, SPARK_VISUAL_SIZE[type] * 0.45)` (game/primitive.ts:127), so the target is a ≥14 px invisible dot per member. That is the canon's *'click an invisible 10 px dot to repair your tower, which is not a fallback'* — a usability trap, not a null path. Say it that way; do not claim 'unrepairable'.

THIS TEST GOES RED BY DESIGN the moment the fix lands — it names `stinkTowerRenderer.ts` as a forbidden publisher. Its own comment says *'A new publisher is not forbidden; it is required to come here and say which class it serves.'* The branch MUST add a fourth `PUBLISHERS` row (:269) and drop the file from this negative list, in the same commit. This is the S177 'tests go red by design — re-pin them, never silence them' rule.

QUESTION 4 ANSWERED. The stink tower IS a star — `isStinkTowerComponent` is `isStarAt(world, squareId, Square, Circle, STINK_TOWER_HUB_DEGREE)` (godlyRecipes/stinkTower.ts:144-146) with `STINK_TOWER_HUB_DEGREE = 3` (constants.ts:3313). This 8-line star walk is exactly the enumeration the cover set needs: hub + 3 leaves + 3 bonds = the recipe's own members, nothing else.

THE HIT BOX'S ANCHOR IS SOUND. A stink tower's motion posture is 'pinned' (`motionPostureOf`), so `d.pos` is rewritten from the anchor primitive EVERY TICK and is a synced field. The sprite is drawn at `d.pos` (stinkTowerRenderer.ts:187), so the hit box must be anchored at `d.pos` too — not at a member centroid, which is what every RAMP_SPECS tower uses. Copying `rampAnchorAtPoint`'s geometry would be wrong.

WITH the manifest this gives the drawn box with no guessing: cell 255×240 at 0.42 = 107.1 × 100.8 px, anchored at footAnchor (0.5, 0.9958) on `d.pos` — i.e. the art STANDS ON `d.pos` and extends ~100 px UP from it. MEASURED off the shipped PNG this session (read-only decode of frame 0/5/11 of row 0): the opaque subject is x 51–202 (152 px wide, centred to within 1 px of the cell) and y 15–239 (225 px tall, bottom flush with the foot). On screen: 63.8 px wide × 94.5 px tall, sitting entirely ABOVE d.pos.

AN EXISTING TEST ASSERTS THE STINK TOWER GETS NO RAMP HIT BOX, and it is CORRECT and must STAY green. This is the strongest argument for putting the new hit test in its OWN function rather than widening `rampAnchorAtPoint`: the fix then never opens `structureRamp.ts` or `structureRamp.test.ts`, which are the two files any parallel ramp lane will touch.

THE CONSEQUENCE TO REPORT, NOT TO FIX HERE. The stink tower is `unitStats: null` (defender.ts:298) so it lands here with `recipeId: null`; `spriteBoxFor` then returns null and the bar hangs at `comp.topY` — the top of the now-INVISIBLE shape cluster (~45 px above the hub), while the tower art's top is ~95 px above it. The bar will draw across the tower's body. ⚠ PRE-EXISTING AND SHARED: `grep -n "RAMP\|rampSpec\|structureRamp" src/render/healthBar.ts` returns NOTHING, so all five S183 ramp towers already have this. Not introduced by this lane.

NO RENDER-ORDER CHANGE IS NEEDED. `structureRenderer.sync` is at :3989 and `stinkTowerRenderer.sync` at :4031, so a mark published by the stink tower in frame N is consumed in frame N+1 — exactly the one-frame lag towerCover.ts:34-38 documents and accepts (16 ms against a 2 s ramp). The consumption side is already fully generic: structureRenderer.ts:167 (`sprite.alpha = coverAlphaForPrim(prim.id)`) and :225 (`const coverAlpha = coverAlphaForBond(bond.id)`) fade ANY id. Publishing is literally the only missing half.

The one new pure function is a `Map`-iteration walk whose only ordering decision is the hit test's tie-break — pin it as "lowest anchor id", explicitly, because `Map` order deciding a player-visible outcome is this codebase's signature defect. The shapes stay SIMULATED, raidable and chewable throughout; only alpha moves (canon §7b, his *"every mechanic from the built connectors is transferred now to the towers"*).
